channel.title: Christopher · Blog & Portfolio
channel.description: Christopher's personal blog and portfolio: creation notes on the Taleb and trading courses, bilingual elementary courses on *The Self-Cultivation of a Leek* and *Rich Dad Poor Dad*, a bilingual general course on *The Turtle Traders' Rules*, Elder's *Trading for a Living* + *The Art of Selling* combined course for kids, reading notes on the Doudou trilogy, investing notes and ten years of practiceNotes. Seven course sites, plus a static blog powered by EmDash CMS.

item.title: He calculated every variable — except how much his conscience could bear
item.description: The first book of Doudou's trilogy is often read as a business-war novel and then set aside. Do the math more carefully and it's actually a cold, clear post-mortem of a failure: an operator who accounted for every rule, every human motive, and every risk control lost to a variable he never put in the model—how much weight a conscience can bear.

item.title: He Didn't Give That Village a Single Cent, Yet Turned the Whole Village Around
item.description: The original novel behind 'Tiandao' (The Way of Heaven). Across the whole Wangmiao Village story, how much money did Ding Yuanying actually put in? Zero. What he gave wasn't money but rules, a market, and a whip — and he himself still had to climb Mount Wutai to ask for permission.

item.title: He gave back a 500,000 bonus, asked only for four words, and finally died in Moscow
item.description: Before he died, Luo Jiaming already held the right answer: see the road but don't walk it. He died anyway. The last book of the trilogy isn't about how to find a path; it's about what else you buy when you copy a ready-made one—exemption from responsibility.

item.title: How This Blog Was Built: Astro + EmDash
item.description: Manage content with EmDash CMS, build static pages with Astro, and publish to Qoder Sites. The admin runs locally, the front end is purely static—a personal-site setup that's both easy to write for and easy to live with.

item.title: A Decade of Life: turn your days into a project
item.description: Health, language, investing, AI—four domains, one dataset, a ten-year scale. Why I built myself a workbench, and what really separates "practice" from "planning."

item.title: The barbell: one end extremely safe, the other extremely risky
item.description: Thales put down a small deposit and rented every olive press — a big win if right, a small loss if wrong. The barbell strategy isn't 50/50 but 90/10: the large portion extremely safe, the small portion extremely bold, the middle ground the most dangerous.

item.title: The turkey's one thousand and first day
item.description: The turkey logged 1,000 days of evidence that 'humans love me'; day 1,001 was Thanksgiving. That things have always been this way doesn't mean they always will be—this is the Black Swan's gentlest and sharpest lesson.

item.title: Dynamic Hedging: A Craft for "Manufacturing Insurance"
item.description: A 460-page trader's manual that is really about the craft of manufacturing insurance: options are the policies, the Greeks are the dashboard, and dynamic hedging is adjusting your position day by day so volatility doesn't bite you.

item.title: Turning Taleb's Incerto series into 12 lessons for children
item.description: Five thick books really answer just one question: the world loves to change its face without warning — what should we do? I broke them into 12 lessons, 32 cards, and a 21-day review schedule, and here I'll explain how the course was designed.
